name: Arizona

law.name: Revised Uniform Athlete Agents Act (A.R.S. 15-1761 to 15-1775). Registration sections repealed in 2017 (Laws 2017, ch. 223).

covers_nil_agents: Yes. A.R.S. 15-1892(E) says anyone who advises or represents an athlete on NIL must follow the athlete agent law. There is still no state registration.
summary: No state license, but the athlete agent law's contract and school-notice rules still apply.

steps.detail: Arizona repealed agent registration in 2017 (A.R.S. 15-1763 to 15-1769). The contract and notice rules still apply.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Make sure the athlete tells the school about an NIL deal before signing
steps.detail: Arizona law says the athlete can't sign an NIL contract before disclosing it to their school.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, any other pay you get, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the Warning to Student Athlete box next to their signature
steps.detail: Use the exact words below, in bold capital letters.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, if that comes first. The athlete must tell the athletic director too.

steps.text: Let the athlete cancel within 14 days
steps.detail: They cancel by written notice. They owe you nothing and keep anything you gave them to sign.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Federal law (SPARTA) bans pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses of clients, every contract and what you spent recruiting each athlete.

steps.text: Never give gifts or money to recruit athletes or make false promises
steps.detail: Don't give anything of value before they sign, or to anyone but the athlete or another agent. Never pre-date or post-date a contract. Breaking this is a class 1 misdemeanor.

steps.text: Warn the athlete before they sign that signing may cost them eligibility
steps.detail: The warning box in the contract does this. Skipping it is a crime in Arizona.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: Statute text was read on azleg.gov and Justia's 2025 Arizona Revised Statutes. A.R.S. 15-1772 and 15-1773 were read on Justia because azleg.gov blocked the request. Confirm them on azleg.gov.
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete. If you sign this contract: 1. You may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport. 2. If you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after entering into this contract or before the next athletic event in which you may participate, whichever comes first, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director. 3. You may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility.
